svg.title: What Each Sensor Actually Watches
svg.desc: Robot photographs © Pololu Corporation — pololu.com. A two-panel RoboLore instructional graphic comparing an encoder and a gyro during the same slipping turn. Neither sensor sees the floor. The encoder watches motor-shaft rotation, while the gyro watches chassis rotation. The white-wheel track photograph and top-view Zumo 32U4 OLED photograph are embedded in their original formats and byte content with editable vector text and arrows.
svg.text: The same turn. Two instruments. Neither one can see the floor.

g.text: The magnet turns 75.81× for every one wheel turn.
the rubber is sliding — and neither sensor measures that
The wheel really did spin that far.
Every number it gave you was true.
It turns with the whole robot, not with either wheel.
the wheels slip — the gyro does not care
It never looked at the wheels at all.

svg.text: A sensor can only tell you about the thing it watches.
